capture.final_message:
Prove all four propositions independently, then form each equivalence from the fact that both sides are true.

- For a finite type with at least three elements, choose three distinct points. Their 3-cycle is a nonidentity even permutation, so it lies in the alternating group; together with the identity this proves the alternating group is nontrivial.
- Use the standard characterization
  \[
  \varphi(p)=p-1 \iff p\text{ is prime}
  \]
  for \(p>0\). The forward direction excludes composites using a nontrivial divisor, while the reverse direction follows because every \(1\le k<p\) is coprime to a prime \(p\). Handle \(p=1\) separately: both statements are false.
- Interpret `Submodule.cardQuot` as the absolute norm. For a nonzero prime ideal \(P\) in a Dedekind domain, norm is multiplicative, hence
  \[
  |S/P^i|=N(P^i)=N(P)^i=|S/P|^i.
  \]
  Equivalently, use the filtration by \(P^k/P^{k+1}\), whose successive factors have the same cardinality as \(S/P\). If the residue field is infinite, separate \(i=0\); for \(i>0\), both sides are represented by `Nat.card = 0`.
- Finally, \( \gcd(n,1)=1 \) is the standard gcd identity, inherited by `PNat`.

The only structurally essential hypothesis is the nonzero prime ideal in a Dedekind domain, which supplies the norm-of-powers formula.
